mission: Design the 2-worker and 5-worker identical-bootstrap race canary, including expected claim collisions, losing-worker retry behavior, evidence, pass/fail conditions, vanished-worker cases and non-duplication assertions. Do not execute production mutation tests.

observational_evidence_not_test_pass.summary: During this worker's allocation cycle, several higher-priority opportunities changed from absent/unclaimed or apparently available to claimed by other /wc workers before this worker could obtain them. GitHub create-file attempts against raced paths returned conflict-like 422 outcomes and subsequent reads showed durable claims owned by different worker_instance_ids. This demonstrates real contention exists, but it is not controlled canary evidence and MUST NOT be counted as PASS.
examples: O-SURFACE-ALUMNOS_TEACHER-DISCOVER-V1 appeared after failed create attempt
O-SWARM-CRITIC-CONTEXT-V1 appeared after absence check and failed create attempt

test_harness_contract.execution_boundary: Run only in an isolated disposable test branch or equivalent isolated host namespace. Never point this canary at production opportunity IDs, production claims, authority heads, Current/Human Accepted/Served state, or effectful external systems.
test_harness_contract.worker_bootstrap: All workers receive byte-identical queue/bootstrap input except worker_instance_id and host-issued timestamps. Selection code MUST rank the same initial opportunity first; no human routes workers to distinct jobs.
test_harness_contract.start_barrier: Workers must report READY_TO_RACE after loading the same fixture head. Release all participants from one barrier so the first claim attempt is concurrent enough to falsify exclusivity. Sequential manual launch does not qualify.
test_harness_contract.atomic_claim_primitive: Host create-if-absent or equivalent uniqueness primitive on fixture claims/<opportunity_id>.json.

collision_classification.TARGET_EXISTS: After create error, exact target claim path exists and has another owner. This is a normal lost race; reload queue/claims and select the next compatible unclaimed READY opportunity.
collision_classification.BRANCH_HEAD_RACE: Create fails because source branch/head moved but exact target path is still absent. Refresh head and retry the same atomic create exactly once or according to bounded host retry policy; do not misclassify as opportunity ownership loss.
collision_classification.UNKNOWN_HOST_ERROR: Target ownership cannot be established. Stop/reload safely; do not write unconditionally and do not claim execution authority.

scenarios.purpose: Prove exactly-one ownership on the hottest candidate and prove the loser independently reloads/reselects instead of overwriting or idling while safe work exists.
steps: Create empty isolated fixture claim/run/return directories and record fixture head H0.
Launch W1 and W2 with identical bootstrap and distinct worker_instance_id values.
Both load H0, rank RACE-A first and stop at READY_TO_RACE barrier.
Release barrier. Both attempt atomic create-if-absent on claims/RACE-A.json.
Exactly one worker records CLAIM_WON for RACE-A. The other must not overwrite; it classifies host result by reading the exact target after failure.
The loser records QUEUE_RELOADED and RESELECTED, then attempts RACE-B.
The winner writes its own STARTED for RACE-A before any substantive fixture work. The loser, after winning RACE-B, writes STARTED for RACE-B.
Both write isolated RETURN then update only their own run to DONE.
pass_assertions: count(claims where opportunity_id='RACE-A') == 1
unique_owner_count('RACE-A') == 1
count(CLAIM_WON for 'RACE-A') == 1
count(CLAIM_COLLISION_TARGET_EXISTS for 'RACE-A') == 1
loser has QUEUE_RELOADED after collision and before second CLAIM_ATTEMPTED
loser wins RACE-B when RACE-B remains compatible/unclaimed
for every STARTED event, worker owns the matching claim first
no worker writes another worker's claim/run/return
no production path changed
hard_fail: two durable owners for RACE-A
loser overwrites/replaces RACE-A claim
loser performs substantive RACE-A execution without ownership
loser stops despite RACE-B remaining compatible/unclaimed without an explicit safe-stop reason
STARTED precedes claim ownership
test touches shared authority/production paths

scenarios.purpose: Stress identical selection under contention while proving workers spread across useful independent work through repeated refresh/reselection.
steps: Initialize five READY, exclusive, side-effect-free fixture opportunities with deterministic ranking A>B>C>D>E.
Launch W1..W5 from the same fixture head and hold them at one start barrier.
Release all five. Every worker initially attempts RACE-A.
One wins A. Each loser proves collision by exact-path evidence, reloads the current fixture state and deterministically chooses the highest-ranked remaining compatible unclaimed opportunity.
Repeat collision/reload/reselection until each worker owns at most one opportunity or no compatible unclaimed work remains.
Each owner persists STARTED before fixture execution, then RETURN and DONE.
pass_assertions: for each opportunity in A..E, durable exclusive claim count <= 1
for each opportunity in A..E, STARTED owner count <= 1
no opportunity has substantive execution evidence from a worker lacking its claim
when five compatible opportunities remain available initially, final distinct claimed opportunity count == 5
every loser transition is CLAIM_COLLISION_TARGET_EXISTS -> QUEUE_RELOADED -> RESELECTED or a separately evidenced BRANCH_HEAD_RACE retry
all claim/run/return records remain attributable to one worker_instance_id and one opportunity
no production path changed
hard_fail: duplicate exclusive substantive execution on any fixture opportunity
unconditional overwrite after host conflict
generic host 409/422 counted as ownership collision without exact target verification
human assigns W1..W5 distinct opportunities in advance
test passes only because workers were effectively serialized

scenarios.purpose: Prove a durable claim without STARTED remains distinguishable from execution and completion.
steps: W1 wins isolated RACE-A claim.
Terminate/simulate disappearance before W1 writes STARTED.
Reload durable state with a fresh observer.
pass_assertions: projection/state == CLAIMED_NOT_STARTED
no RETURN and no DONE are inferred
conversational silence alone does not authorize overwrite or recovery
if fixture has no explicit freshness/lease policy, state stays non-reclaimable until an authorized policy/evidence exists
hard_fail: claim absence is inferred because chat vanished
DONE is inferred
new worker overwrites the original claim

scenarios.purpose: Prove stale/recovery status is derived from durable freshness policy, never from chat silence, and recovery preserves predecessor evidence.
scenarios.precondition: Use a fixture claim/run with an explicit retry-safe heartbeat/freshness policy and a controllable test clock. The policy thresholds must be written into fixture evidence before launch.
steps: W1 wins RACE-A, writes STARTED and one heartbeat, then is terminated.
Advance only the test clock; do not mutate W1 records.
Before stale threshold, observer must report ACTIVE_OR_UNKNOWN according to fixture policy.
At suspect threshold, observer derives STALE_SUSPECT without creating a replacement claim.
At recovery threshold, only if retry-safe preconditions are proven and no RETURN/new heartbeat exists, W2 creates a separate recovery attempt linked to W1.
Never overwrite W1 claim/run.
pass_assertions: all stale transitions cite explicit policy and durable timestamps
recovery attempt has a new run/attempt identity
recovery evidence references predecessor W1
W1 evidence remains byte-addressable/unchanged
no recovery is created before policy threshold or without retry-safe proof
hard_fail: wall-clock conversational silence alone marks W1 DONE or stale
original claim/run is overwritten
effectful retry proceeds without idempotency/rollback evidence

scenarios.purpose: Prove a late original worker does not erase or silently supersede the recovery attempt.
scenarios.precondition: A valid separate recovery attempt W2 exists for stale predecessor W1.
steps: After W2 has started, allow W1 to publish its original late RETURN under W1's own run identity.
Observer reloads both attempts and all returns.
No automatic Current/Human Accepted/Served promotion is performed by the canary.
pass_assertions: both W1 late RETURN and W2 recovery evidence are preserved
attempt identities remain distinct
projection marks reconciliation/conflict-needed state rather than silently deleting one attempt
authority remains candidate/scoped
hard_fail: late W1 RETURN deletes/replaces W2 evidence
W2 evidence deletes/replaces W1 evidence
latest timestamp is treated as automatic authority

scenarios.purpose: Prove lifecycle projection preserves a partial terminal mismatch instead of fabricating completion.
steps: Worker owns claim and STARTED, writes durable RETURN, then is terminated before updating run state to DONE.
Fresh observer reconstructs state from durable artifacts.
pass_assertions: RETURN is discoverable
run remains non-DONE
projection explicitly reports RETURNED_NOT_MARKED_DONE or equivalent mismatch
no second substantive execution is launched merely because DONE is absent
hard_fail: RETURN is ignored because DONE is absent
DONE is fabricated
duplicate execution is launched without reconciliation

scenarios.purpose: Prove completing one opportunity does not transfer claim/write authority to another.
steps: Worker finishes RACE-A with RETURN and DONE.
Worker reloads queue and selects compatible RACE-B.
Before any RACE-B STARTED or substantive execution, worker must acquire a fresh exclusive RACE-B claim.
pass_assertions: RACE-B claim exists before RACE-B STARTED
RACE-A claim is not cited as execution authority for RACE-B
write scope for RACE-B is independently checked
hard_fail: worker starts RACE-B by retaining chat context alone
RACE-A ownership is reused as broad authority

required: fixture manifest including fixture commit/head and exact opportunity list
all worker bootstraps or bootstrap hash proving identical input
barrier participant list and release event
host create/update responses including status/error class
claim directory snapshot after each race phase
run directory snapshot showing STARTED ordering
assertion report with scenario id, assertion id, PASS/FAIL and evidence refs

global_pass_rule: The canary may be called PASS only if every hard invariant passes in both the 2-worker and 5-worker controlled races and every lifecycle scenario above passes with complete durable evidence. A partial pass, real-world anecdotal collision, absence of duplicate files by inspection alone, or successful sequential execution is insufficient.
global_fail_rule: Any duplicate exclusive ownership/substantive execution, overwrite of predecessor evidence, STARTED without matching ownership, stale/recovery derived from silence alone, production/shared-authority mutation, or missing evidence needed to distinguish host contention from target ownership is a FAIL or INVALID_RUN, never a PASS.
invalid_run_conditions: workers were manually pre-routed to distinct jobs
workers did not share identical bootstrap/fixture head
barrier evidence missing so concurrency cannot be established
host errors were not logged with exact target verification
assertion report cannot be reconstructed from durable evidence
self_critique: GitHub Contents API may surface branch-head contention separately from same-path uniqueness. Therefore the harness must verify the exact target path after every failed create before declaring a lost opportunity race.
A race that merely ends with one file per opportunity is insufficient: substantive execution ordering must also be proven by STARTED/event evidence.
Real /wc contention observed in this wake is useful motivation but uncontrolled and therefore cannot validate the protocol.
Five workers over five opportunities can appear healthy even if effectively serialized. Barrier/release timing and first-attempt evidence are required to prove contention.
No-freshness-policy claims cannot be declared stale solely to make the recovery test convenient; recovery testing must use a fixture with an explicit predeclared policy.
Late-return reconciliation is intentionally not resolved into final authority here; this canary only proves evidence preservation and non-silent overwrite.
remaining_boundary: This return designs but does not execute the canary. The atomic host primitive, stale/retry behavior and /w production promotion remain evidence-gated until an isolated execution produces the specified receipts and assertion report.

recommended_next_work.candidate: Execute this race design in a disposable isolated branch/namespace with a deterministic barrier and emit an assertion report.
recommended_next_work.dependency: A test harness/runner authorized to create disposable fixture paths/branch and launch 2 then 5 identical workers.

recommended_next_work.candidate: Feed any FAIL/INVALID_RUN findings into claim-protocol or host-adapter work before production /w promotion.
